title: Linkage disequilibrium and allelic heterogeneity explain variation in coronary artery disease risk at 9p21 across populations and reduced effect in Africans.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. The Europe PMC full-text fetch for the linked PMC record failed. I read the medRxiv preprint full text (first 100k characters) for the cohorts used and the data access route.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The cohorts come from the preprint: UK Biobank (application 87255), Biobank Japan, MVP (Million Veteran Program), H3Africa/AWI-Gen and a Saudi hospital cohort (KFSHRC). Sample sizes are in a supplementary table S0 I did not see. I found no public deposit of summary statistics.

a1_downloadable.note: Every cohort's individual-level genotypes and case/control status are controlled access: UK Biobank, MVP and Biobank Japan need applications, H3Africa goes through EGA (European Genome-phenome Archive) and KFSHRC is an institutional cohort. I found no public summary statistics. Seen in the preprint text only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked because the data is inaccessible. The coronary artery disease case/control label would sit in each biobank's phenotype tables, behind the same access controls.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; the genotypes are controlled access.

a5_enough_rows.note: Sample sizes are in supplementary table S0, which I did not see.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. The labels would be clinical CAD (coronary artery disease) diagnoses, which are not model outputs.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible without applying for access to UK Biobank, MVP (Million Veteran Program), Biobank Japan and H3Africa data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the genotypes at one chromosome 9 region, with ancestry, to predict coronary artery disease risk in different populations.
plain_idea.train_on: Individual genotypes and local-ancestry calls at 9p21.3 (a region on chromosome 9) from multi-ancestry biobanks; the number of people is unknown (in a table I could not see).
plain_idea.predict: Whether each person has coronary artery disease, taken from biobank clinical records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could show whether haplotype-aware models (models that read the combination of variants inherited together) recover the risk signal in people of African ancestry that single-variant tests miss.

ml_idea: Haplotype-level CAD (coronary artery disease) risk model at 9p21.3, with transfer across ancestries. It is blocked because all individual-level data is controlled access.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the data is inaccessible.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check the data availability statement for any deposited 9p21 per-ancestry summary statistics; according to the preprint text none appear to exist.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: all cohorts are controlled access (UK Biobank, MVP, Biobank Japan, H3Africa via the European Genome-phenome Archive) and I found no public summary statistics. Flag as controlled access.
